clinician.trajectory_summary: A 75-year-old woman presented with vomit, diarrhea, confusion, epigastric pain, and weight loss, with a history of chronic renal insufficiency and other comorbidities. Initial lab analysis revealed severe hyponatremia (124 mmol/L), hypokalemia (3.1 mmol/L), acute kidney injury (creatininemia 318.24 μmol/L, hyperazotemia 188 mg/dl), and leukocytosis. The patient also experienced persistent, mucous diarrhea. A colonoscopy identified a giant rectal polyp (8-9 cm, occupying three quarters of the luminal circumference). Biopsy confirmed this to be a villous adenoma with focal high-grade dysplasia. Staging CT showed no signs of mural involvement, sphincterial/mesorectal involvement, or distant metastases. Electrolyte imbalances and creatinine normalized after 10 days of intravenous rehydration and potassium infusion. An intra-operative frozen section pathological examination showed involvement of the distal margin by intramucosal adenocarcinoma.
